summary.text: A 79-year-old woman presented with a thigh hematoma, subcutaneous bleeding in both hands and hematuria. She had no history of anticoagulant or antiplatelet use and no personal or family history of bleeding disorders.

The cross-mixing test failed to correct the aPTT, FVIII activity was undetectable (<0.9%) and the FVIII inhibitor titer was 124 BU/mL, while the vWF antigen and activity were normal. Acquired hemophilia A was diagnosed and she was started on prednisolone 65 mg/day and cyclophosphamide 50 mg/day with aPCC, and bleeding symptoms and laboratory findings gradually improved.

On hospital day 23 she was diagnosed with acute cholecystitis, with the aPTT still prolonged (66 s), FVIII activity persistently low (4.4%) and a high FVIII inhibitor titer (52 BU/mL). Invasive interventions were deemed inappropriate and antibiotics were started. Endoscopic nasobiliary gallbladder drainage attempted on hospital day 26 was unsuccessful because gallbladder cannulation failed, so endoscopic nasobiliary drainage was performed instead. Worsening abdominal pain followed on day 27.

Plasma exchange was started to eliminate the FVIII inhibitors and correct coagulation function before surgery. After 3 PE sessions the aPTT was 47 s, FVIII activity 12%, FVIII inhibitor titer 2 BU/mL and ACT 160 s. Laparoscopic cholecystectomy on hospital day 30 showed a completely gangrenous gallbladder with bile leakage and localized peritonitis, with minimal blood loss.

aPCC was given on PODs 2, 4 and 5 and no additional plasma exchange was required. The postoperative course was uneventful and she was discharged on POD 16. By the 2-month follow-up the FVIII inhibitor had been eliminated and the aPTT and FVIII activity had normalized; immunosuppressive therapy was discontinued at 4 months after surgery and remission has been maintained.

article_limitations: Single case report; the narrative aPTT (>200 s) conflicts with Table 1 aPTT 68.4 s at diagnosis and both are review-only.
Figure 1, 3, 5 and 6 plot serial values and treatment doses; those pixel readings are recorded in the visual submission, not as text facts.

Considered-but-not-given therapies (rituximab, rFVIIa) and interventions deemed inappropriate at cholecystitis onset (cholecystectomy, percutaneous transhepatic gallbladder drainage) are recorded as absent, never as given.
Table 1 values carry no flags because none are stated beyond the text calls for PT, platelet count, vWF and lupus anticoagulant.
Figure 5 aPCC dose boxes sit over postoperative day 2 and days 4 to 5 on the chart, consistent with the text PODs 2, 4 and 5; chart positions are not used as fact times.
